title: feat(ui): share inline media and copyable code blocks
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Extracts the shared Markdown and CodeBlock changes from website v2 (#14472), including the media rendering merged in #14813.
- Keeps images, audio and video inline; supports the existing generated-media links without file extensions.
- Adds labelled, wrapping code blocks using the existing copy button.
- Three files only: no website pages, global styles, dependencies or auth changes.
- Verified all 23 UI tests, TypeScript, full SDK/UI builds and Biome.

gist.headline: Media stays in the garden
gist.blurb: Markdown can now keep its images, audio, and video right where the conversation put them. Code blocks also gained labels, wrapping, and a copy button—because scrolling sideways is not a personality trait.
gist.summary: The shared UI Markdown renderer now displays inline images, audio, and video—including generated-media URLs without file extensions—and adds labelled, wrapping CodeBlock components with the existing copy control.
gist.impact: Apps using the shared UI can present generated media directly in Markdown and give readers readable, one-click-copyable code snippets without sending them away to a link.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy shared Markdown workbench: Polli tends a little code-garden where an image, audio waveform, and video thumbnail bloom inline from one document, while a labelled code scroll wraps neatly beside a chunky copy-button stamp. The scene represents media remaining embedded in the reading flow and code becoming easier to scan and reuse.
